name: Team Configuration Neutrality

positioning.oneLineSummary: Stops solo-founder and technical-title heuristics from replacing direct assessment of team coverage, execution, key-person risk, and governance.
positioning.productLabel: Team Configuration Anti-Gate — based on Super Founders public findings
notAClaimOf: equal execution risk for every team size
technical capability being optional in technical companies

attribution.display: Based on Ali Tamaseb's public solo-founder and founder-composition findings

neutralParaphrase: In the author's selected comparison groups, solo-founder status and simple technical versus non-technical title combinations did not justify mechanical rejection. The product should evaluate whether the actual team covers present and next-stage work, survives key-person failure, makes decisions, recruits, and governs conflict; it should not add an opposite preference for solo or non-technical founders.

locator.value: Solo founders section: comparison with venture-funded non-unicorn group
Interview discussion of 20 percent solo-founder prevalence in both selected groups
Transcript discussion of technical/non-technical founding-team combinations and warning against proxy rules
Decision-under-uncertainty discussion on estimates and uncertainty

requiredConditions: Team-size labels are kept separate from capability evidence.
Stage- and sector-specific work is explicitly mapped.
The conclusion does not claim configuration equivalence.

requiredEvidence.description: Named ownership of product, technology, customer, hiring, finance, regulation, and operations responsibilities.
Dated examples of the current team delivering and coordinating stage-critical work.
Operational, technical, commercial, and signing-control dependence on individual people.
Founder equity, vesting, roles, decision rights, conflict history, and board expectations.

decisionQuestions: Which necessary work is uncovered regardless of founder count?
What breaks if one key person is unavailable?
Does a title such as technical CEO reflect demonstrable capability?
How does the team resolve decisions and conflict?
Can missing capability be recruited before it becomes a binding constraint?
Would the team judgment change if founder count were hidden?
positiveSignals: All stage-critical responsibilities have credible owners.
The team has delivered cross-functional milestones.
Key-person dependencies are known and mitigated.
Governance and vesting support continued cooperation.
redFlags: Solo status alone causes rejection or admiration.
A technical or business title is accepted without work evidence.
Multiple founders obscure missing ownership or unresolved conflict.
One person controls customers, code, credentials, finance, and decisions without continuity.
The hiring plan assumes scarce capability will appear after financing.
disconfirmingEvidence: A stage-critical responsibility repeatedly fails for lack of capacity.
Reference checks show unresolved founder conflict.
IP, customer, or system access is not assigned to the company.
Hiring evidence contradicts the stated ability to fill gaps.
Governance creates deadlock or unchecked key-person control.
contraindications: Do not infer equal risk from an absence of detected group difference.
Do not waive sector-specific technical, licensing, or safety capability.
Do not treat cofounder count as a formal score.

instructions: Hide founder count and technical labels during the first capability review.
Map responsibilities, evidence of execution, continuity, and governance.
Reveal configuration and test whether it creates specific, evidenced risk.
Separate uncovered work from configuration preference.
Conclude on team coverage and risk, not ideal founder count.

sourceReliability.low: Only folklore about ideal cofounder count is available.
sourceReliability.medium: Author public findings support removing a hard gate.
sourceReliability.high: Licensed estimates, uncertainty, and matched external validation are reviewed.

evidenceStrength.medium: Responsibility map and some observed execution exist.
evidenceStrength.high: Execution, references, continuity, governance, and recruiting evidence converge.

evidenceCoverage.low: Responsibilities or key-person dependencies are unknown.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Current coverage is known but next-stage hiring or governance is incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: Current and next-stage work, continuity, hiring, equity, and conflict are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: Founding-team configuration is no longer a material uncertainty.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: The company is later stage but retains key-person risk.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Early-stage delivery depends directly on the founding team.

judgmentConfidence.medium: The hard gate is removed but some capability risk is unresolved.
judgmentConfidence.high: Configuration-neutral assessment and operational evidence converge.

promotionRequirements: Validate configuration-neutral capability rubric by stage and sector.
Test incremental value beyond observed execution and governance.
empiricalQualifications: The public no-disadvantage finding applies to selected venture-funded groups.
No detected difference does not prove exact equivalence.
Configuration can affect bandwidth and key-person risk even if it is not a universal success predictor.

rights.notes: No book or interview passage is reproduced.

openIssues: Complete licensed statistical review of founder-count and composition findings.
Reconcile governance lens with The Founder's Dilemmas.
